# Pariññāvāra (Ya 6.3)
**ID:** Ya 6.3
**Section:** Yamaka (ya)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pariññāvāra* (Ya 6.3) is a canonical section of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. In the overall compositional scheme of the *Yamaka*, doctrinal categories derived from fundamental doctrinal matrices (*mātikā*) are systematically investigated through paired questions and answers distributed across three standard divisions: the designation section (*paññatti-vāra*), the process section (*pavatti-vāra*), and the comprehension section (*pariññā-vāra*) [Anderson 1999; Ronkin 2005].
While the preceding *pavatti-vāra* treats phenomenal occurrence and rebirth processes, the *pariññāvāra* examines the extent or degree to which a given individual or class of beings understands and comprehends the doctrinal category under consideration [Norman 1983; Anderson 1999]. The questioning in this division relies predominantly on the verb *parijānāti* ("to comprehend" or "to know accurately") [Anderson 1999]. In the context of the *Yamaka*'s interrogative framework, "penetration" or "comprehension" (*pariññā*) signifies the penetrating insight realized at the moment of entering into the stages of holiness [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Scholars note that the *Yamaka*'s dialectical structure appears designed to instill full competency in students who have already mastered the doctrinal system, suggesting it may represent one of the later strata of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Norman 1983].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus reports any cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus shows extensive internal reuse across the *Yamaka*, identifying 37 matching passages shared with two other canonical texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest reuse partner is the corresponding *Pariññāvāra* of Ya 7.2.4 (35 matches, 4,409 shared characters; longest match §1.1–2.1 ↔ §398.1–399.1), along with minor structural formula overlap with the *Paccuppannavāra* (Ya 2.3.1) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language [SuttaCentral].

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Pariññāvāra (Ya 7.2.4) (§1.1–2.1 ↔ §398.1–399.1); Paccuppannavāra (Ya 2.3.1) (§0.2–3.1 ↔ §0.2–3.1)
